Mapping Entropy

Source: R/centrality-batch67.R
centrality_mapping_entropy.Rd

Mapping entropy (ME; Nie et al. 2016) weighs the logarithms of the degree centralities of a node's neighbors by the node's own degree centrality: $$ME_i = -DC_i \sum_{j \in N(i)} \log DC_j, \qquad DC_i = \frac{k_i}{N - 1},$$ with \(k\) the degree and \(N\) the number of nodes.

Usage

centrality_mapping_entropy(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The source cites degree centrality for \(DC\) without giving a formula; \(DC\) is the degree divided by \(N - 1\), the usual degree centrality. Only with this reading is the source's equation (1) an entropy, and only with it does removing the nodes in decreasing order of the score beat removing them by degree on the two networks of the source's Table 1 that could be checked, as the source reports. The score is then never negative and grows with the degree. The Centrality Zoo and Omar and Plapper (2021) use the raw degree, which makes every score zero or negative and ranks low-degree nodes first; the two readings order the nodes differently, not on another scale. The logarithm is natural; the base only rescales. centrality_local_entropy is equation (2) of the same source with the raw degree, a different quantity: the two have Kendall correlations between -0.56 and -0.27 on four test networks. The score ranks nodes in nearly the reverse order of local_bridging (mean Kendall correlation -0.98 over the four networks, -0.97 at the least) and much like the degree (0.88 to 0.93).. The source prints no score, so the implementation is checked against the definition only. Isolated nodes, and the node of a one-node network, score 0. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Nie, T., Guo, Z., Zhao, K. and Lu, Z. (2016). Using mapping entropy to identify node centrality in complex networks. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 453, 290-297. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2016.02.009 .

See also

centrality_local_entropy, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_mapping_entropy(regulation_net)
